title: Barát-Thomassen Conjecture (Conjecture 1.1)
statement_text: For any fixed tree $T$, there is an integer $c_T$ such that every $c_T$-edge-connected graph with its number of edges divisible by $|E(T)|$ can be $T$-decomposed.
context_text: Barát and Thomassen raised this conjecture in 2006, asserting that highly edge-connected graphs can be decomposed into copies of any fixed tree. The conjecture was fully solved by the current authors and Merker [1]; the present paper focuses on the path case and seeks an alternative proof under weaker hypotheses.
paper_contribution: Provides an alternative proof of the path case ($T = P_\ell$) with a strictly weaker hypothesis: every 24-edge-connected graph with minimum degree at least $d_\ell$ admits a decomposition into paths of length $\ell$ (plus at most one shorter path), with edge-connectivity constant and independent of $\ell$; also proves the bound drops to 4 for eulerian graphs.

title: Conjecture 1.2
statement_text: There is a function $f$ such that, for any fixed tree $T$ with maximum degree $\Delta_T$, every $f(\Delta_T)$-edge-connected graph with its number of edges divisible by $|E(T)|$ and minimum degree at least $f(|E(T)|)$ can be $T$-decomposed.
context_text: For graphs $G$ and $H$ with $|E(H)|$ dividing $|E(G)|$, $G$ is $H$-decomposable ($H$-decomposed) if $E(G)$ can be partitioned into sets $E_1,\dots,E_k$ each inducing an isomorphic copy of $H$. The Barát–Thomassen conjecture states that for every fixed tree $T$ there is $c_T$ such that every $c_T$-edge-connected graph with number of edges divisible by $|E(T)|$ has a $T$-decomposition; it was proved by the authors with Merker, but the essentially probabilistic proof gives a huge, far from optimal, edge-connectivity bound. The present conjecture is the authors' refinement, asserting that the edge-connectivity can be lowered to a constant depending only on the maximum degree $\Delta_T$ of $T$, provided this is offset by a large minimum degree. The authors prove it when $\Delta_T\le2$, i.e. for paths: for every $\ell\ge2$ there is $d_\ell$ such that every $24$-edge-connected graph with minimum degree at least $d_\ell$ decomposes into paths of length $\ell$ (edges) plus one additional path of length at most $\ell$, so $f(2)\le24$; they also show $f(2)\ge3$, since there are $2$-edge-connected graphs of arbitrarily large minimum degree with no decomposition into paths of length $9$.
